Episode 190. Mariette Hister's Champion (6)
Jin and Valeria were walking on the beach.
The sea surrounding Honka Island, outside the Champion’s domain, was dyed in the sunset, and each wave shimmered like a glowing gem.
-[I, have never, seen it, but the evening and night scenery of the island, is said to be, beautiful. Champions, go out and wait while enjoying the breeze. It's a bit, chaotic, here.]
The golem had spoken not long after the rock, paper, scissors test was over. Zen and Teben were making a fuss about the parts they needed to take care of before giving the communication device.
Neither of them minded being made to take an unplanned walk for that reason.
Their footprints were spreading over the wet sand. The pleasant sea scent tickled their noses, and the cool wind rustled their hair.
"Shall we dip up to our ankles?"
Surprisingly, it was Valeria who suggested this, removing her shoes. Jin nodded and stepped onto the gently breaking wave with his bare feet.
Walking together like this reminded him of the good old times in their past lives.
Sometimes as a master and disciple, sometimes as friends, and sometimes feeling even closer as they roamed the world.
However, looking back, even then, they each had a loneliness in their hearts that they did not show to each other.

Jin was filled with a desire for revenge against his clan and the desire for success derived from it, and Valeria often behaved like someone ready to leave at any time because of the Hister's mission.
They both didn't want to get hurt.

Jin lost Gilly by being exiled, and Valeria lost the gray owl she had in her childhood. Both of them had tried not to give their hearts too deeply to anyone else because of their memories of losing their families.
But now it's different. They were both completely open to each other and walking together.
"I feel like I've been feeling good a lot recently. I'd forgotten that feeling for a long time before I met you and the other comrades."
"For you, the revenge on Zipfel and the mission as a Hister must have been everything."

"Of course, even now, those are the most important parts of my life. But I'm feeling that the world is not something to live alone in. If I had been walking alone looking at this beautiful scenery, I wouldn't feel as good as now. I'd probably feel lonely."
Valeria had many such moments. While wandering the world as a fugitive from a young age, she often explored all kinds of mysterious spaces untouched by human hands alone.
But she never felt as moved as she does now, no matter what spectacular scenery she faced. Even the most beautiful places were no different from colorless landscapes.
Jin had never seen this honest side of Valeria in their past lives. He felt a strange flutter inside him and turned his gaze to the distance for a moment.
"You've grown a lot. Thinking about the time from when we first met in Mamit to settling down in Tikan."
"Let's just say it was puberty. I feel a little embarrassed when I think about how I was back then."
"Are you going to be more supportive to other comrades now?"
"I plan to try. Even when I acted uncooperatively at first, the comrades had always cared for me."
"Really? How are you going to try? Can you really do it?"
"Stop teasing."
"Alright."
Small crabs were scattering at their feet. The two sat for a while watching them and also gazing blankly at the sun sinking little by little into the sea.
"Jin."
"Hmm?"
"There are times when I feel like meeting you was destined."
Caught off guard by the unexpected topic, Jin almost coughed in surprise.
"……Destiny?"
"In Mamit, when I saw you, I immediately said your name. Do you remember?"
"I remember."

"By that time, you were already famous because of the Holy Nation incident, so even when I called you by name as if I knew you, you didn't seem surprised. But in fact, I saw you before the world knew about you."
"……You were watching me?"
"I had a dream. For some reason, I was dreaming almost every day about you."
Are you just going to lie there?
Shut up.
Pathetic. Your proud brothers will love you, Jin.
Who are you? How do you know my name?
You still have curiosity left in you. It seems you still cling to this world. Follow me, I'll forgive you for threatening the person who tried to help you with a knife.
As Valeria explained the contents of her dream, Jin's eyes widened.
"You... dreamed about that continuously?"
The dream was exactly the same moment as when Jin first met Valeria in her past life.
"In addition to that, among the records I found in the previous Hall of Records, there was one from 1795 and 1799 that predicted a person would come looking for me in Mamit. That person was you."
"A record predicting the future? Is that even possible?"

"If it's a fully developed record magic, it's possible, although limited. But unlike Azmill's foresight, just because you peeked at the records of the future doesn't mean the future is determined. If I didn't wait for you in Mamit knowing the records, we couldn't have met."
Jin couldn't help but feel more shocked.
According to Valeria, there were records that surpassed his regression. The dream Valeria had was a record of her past life, and Jin coming to Mamit was a record of the present.
"You seem quite surprised."
"I couldn't help it."

"I thought all those dreams and future records were destiny and a contingency left by my ancestors. Probably, in the future records that my ancestors saw, it was mentioned that I needed you to reach the end of my mission."
The root of the Hister family, the clues about the fairy tribe, and the encounter with Lert would all have been impossible without Jin.
"And after I met you, occasionally. I felt like you knew me well."
-With a lot of peppers and onions, a steamed lamb dish, and a beef offal stew. Make sure to put enough pepper in this. And......

Before they went to Wantaromo forest together, the food Jin ordered in the restaurant was the favorite food of the grey owls. Naturally, it was also the food that Jin and Valeria often ate together in their past life.
"It was a common combination, but it was strange that Jin had ordered the exact same food down to the details.
Valeria stopped in her tracks and turned to look at Jin.
"Jin. You have a secret too, don't you?"
Jin locked eyes with her, pondering how to respond.
But Valeria hadn't asked to hear an answer. She was recalling the record that Jin 'had once died'.
"I'm sure that whatever secret you have, it won't harm me, or the world."
"Valeria."
"And I feel like I will someday examine all records about you. Then, even if it's a bit embarrassing, I hope you won't reject my magic."
The sunset was ending.
Valeria, soaked in the last red light poured out by the sun, smiled broadly.
At her appearance, Jin momentarily forgot everything he had just heard.

He forgot even to breathe, unable to take his eyes off Valeria. The scent of the sea in her hair became clear, making his head spin, and everything else around blurred except for the sight of Valeria.
He took one step towards Valeria. Unconsciously two steps, three steps, close enough that their noses could touch.
Valeria opened her arms and embraced Jin. Their cheeks were so hot they could melt. The sun had just set, and a calm darkness enveloped the island.
"……I'm glad I met you, Jin."
"Me too."
For some reason, his throat constricted, Jin answered like that.
The two returned to the shrine when dawn was almost over. Only then had Teben and Zen finished fixing the communication device, and Honka and Shuri conveyed that news.
[We have been waiting for a long time, successors. Did you have a good time?]
Jin and Valeria showed somewhat awkward faces to the golem.
[You seemed to enjoy the walk. The master said there are many beautiful places on our Honka Island.]
[Heh, who goes for a nearly ten-hour walk? This is called a date, golem. Ancestors should give us some work…… well, we're losers so we don't have complaints.]
[Yes, we really don't have any complaints. As long as you tell us in detail how you two, who look so serious, spent your time.]
[It is not, polite, to ask such things.]
[What? Politeness? You should stay in the shrine for three hundred and fifty years like us! How much fun this kind of story is!]
[I too, have only been in the shrine. For even longer. And, other people's, love stories. Are usually, fun stories.]
[Teben, I hate that golem!]
[I hate it too!]
[If you dislike, come at me, I will face you, anytime.]
Zen and Teben, who were acting tough, cautiously avoided the golem's eyes and showed the communication device."
The communication device was an object shaped like a square plate, and there were a total of three.
[It's a long-range communication device. It's something that allows lovers to converse even if they are at the ends of the world....]
[Tsk... The thought of you guys nagging at me all the time with this makes my whole body twist. But rejoice! Descendant, you must have been walking a lonely road so far.]
"I don't plan to use it for that purpose, but thank you, ancestor."
[What!? You won't use it for that purpose? Then I won't give it. Lovers need to talk frequently!]
[Not giving it? Again, you're showing an unsightly side, Teben. Are you still not able to accept your defeat? You really are something.]
Jin and Valeria laughed at the harmless foolish appearance of the two.

[The usage and manufacturing methods are all detailed in this manual. Right now, these three are all we have, but if you have the materials and a high-level engineer, you can make more. Now go! We're going to devote ourselves to rock-paper-scissors training again.]
[Having passed on the long-held burden, I can be more at ease, tsk.]
Looking at the manual, Jin handed one of the communication devices back to Zen and Teben.
"I think it would be good if you two communicate with us often. With the golem."
"We'll tell you stories from the outside world whenever you're bored. Right now, that's the only way we can repay our ancestors."
At those words, Zen and Teben seemed on the verge of shedding tears.
[Is that true?]
[We're just lowly losers... Are you going to bestow such recognition?]
"You are not lowly at all, ancestors. We're getting so much from this succession site thanks to you. Compared to the toil you've endured over the past 350 years... I've done nothing."
[Our descendant, you're the best!]
[Neither of you are my descendants, but you're the best!]
Teben and Zen hugged the two of them and danced joyfully. Then Valeria locked eyes with the golem.
"I'm going to name you."
[Oh... Finally, I, have a name. Hurry, hurry, decide.]
"Elo Hister."
The golem stood motionless for a moment without a word.
Worried that it didn't like inheriting the name Elo to honor Marliet, Valeria had a moment of worry, but it was unnecessary.
The golem's eyes were streaming with magic power, like tears.
[A name, given by the grace of my master. And the surname of the lineage. I'm touched. I am now Elo Hister, a member of the Hister family.]
"I'm glad you like it. I look forward to working with you, Elo."
The golem, no, Elo, seemed embarrassed as he scratched the back of his head and shook hands with Valeria. Then he took something out from his pocket and handed it over.
[This is, my, blueprint. Please make my, brother. The other one...is your, master's, vision magic book.]
In addition to the communication device, Elo's blueprint and a vision magic book.
The journey through Marliet's succession site ended so richly.
